item.research_question: How can a high-entropy alloy be designed to simultaneously achieve high yield strength and high crack-initiation fracture toughness, overcoming the typical trade-off between these properties?
item.material_system: Al0.5CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy (composition: Cr ~22.5%, Co ~24.6%, Fe ~23.2%, Ni ~24.5%, Al ~5.21 wt%)
item.processing_route: Laser powder-bed fusion (L-PBF) additive manufacturing using an Nd:YAG fiber laser (300 W power, 50 µm layer thickness, 90 µm hatch spacing, 500 mm.s−1 scanning speed) followed by optional heat treatments (e.g., 750 °C for 1 h)
item.test_conditions: Tensile tests at 298 K and 77 K with strain rate 10−3 s−1; Fracture toughness tests (C(T) specimens) at 298 K and 77 K using J-integral-based R-curves
key_findings: Yield strength (σy) of as-printed alloy is ~729 ± 31 MPa at 298 K and ~942 ± 11 MPa at 77 K.
Crack-initiation fracture toughness (KJIc) is ~306 MPa√m at 298 K and ~290 MPa√m at 77 K.
The as-printed alloy shows ~47% higher KJIc than wrought CrCoNi at 298 K.
The as-printed alloy shows ~66% higher yield strength than wrought CrCoNi at 298 K.
Heat treatment (HT3: 750 °C, 1 h) increases yield strength to ~1090 MPa at 298 K but reduces KJIc to ~135 MPa√m.
At 77 K, the heat-treated alloy exhibits unstable crack growth with KJIc dropping to ~51 MPa√m.
Dislocation bands spread up to ~300 µm away from the crack tip in the as-printed honeycomb microstructure.
Nano-twinning is activated at 77 K in the as-printed alloy, with twin growth restricted by B2 phase boundaries.
item.mechanism: The nano-bridged honeycomb microstructure provides strength via the ordered B2 phase and high dislocation density, while the dislocation nano-bridges connecting the B2 phase on cell boundaries act as highways for dislocation movement away from the crack tip, facilitating crack blunting and shielding to enhance intrinsic toughness.
item.limitations: Conventional heat treatments that form uniformly distributed B2 precipitates restrict dislocation movement away from the crack tip, leading to a significant reduction in fracture toughness (e.g., ~5.7 times lower at 77 K compared to the as-printed state).
item.future_work: Manipulating the thermal gradient (G) and solidification rate (R) during 3D printing to alter the size of the honeycomb cells and tailor the material's strength and fracture toughness for specific applications.
quotes: The dislocation nano-bridge form in the regions of the cell boundaries where solutes (Al/Ni) concentration was insufficient to the form B2 phase.
during severe plastic deformation, the dislocation movement away from the crack tip is facilitated to improve the fracture resistance through blunting and shielding of the crack tip.
